$schema_note: Mock extracted SOP/policy document for Coles Knowledge Agent ingestion. Represents the identity-verification and voice-channel action-scoping policy that governs which Voice Agent request types are eligible for auto-execution versus human approval. Consumed by Knowledge Agent and referenced by the Voice Agent's deterministic policy-check step (intent classification -> slot filling -> policy check -> ITSM action, per Voice_Assist.pdf and voice_assist_context_2 §1/§6 A16).
title: Voice Channel Identity Verification & Action Scoping Policy

source_document.ingestion_pipeline: AI Search hybrid ingestion (chunked, embedded, indexed)

summary: Defines which caller identity-verification method is required before any Voice Agent action, and which request types are approved for straight-through (auto-execute) resolution versus those that must always be routed for human approval, per the closed-set action policy (Voice Agent never infers a new action type).

sections.heading: Caller Identity Verification (Mandatory, Pre-Agent-Turn)
sections.content: All callers must pass deterministic identity verification via Microsoft Entra ID before the Voice Agent processes any request-related intent. Verification is a challenge of employee ID plus one secondary factor (date of birth or line manager name, selected at random per call). Verification is never performed by the LLM — it is a deterministic service check that gates the conversation before any agent reasoning turn begins. A failed verification after two attempts ends the automated flow and routes to a human agent.

sections.heading: Auto-Execute Eligible Request Types
sections.content: The following request types are approved for straight-through voice-channel auto-execution, provided caller verification has passed and no elevated/privileged account flags are present on the target account: (a) Standard corporate Entra account password reset, (b) Store POS terminal login/PIN reset, (c) Incident creation for any store-level hardware or service fault (no approval needed to log an incident). These are narrow, low-risk, reversible actions with an existing automatable API (Entra ID / MIM) and have been explicitly approved for auto-execution per the progressive autonomy policy.

sections.heading: Approval-Required Request Types
sections.content: The following request types must always be routed to a human approver and are never auto-executed by the Voice Agent, regardless of caller verification outcome: (a) Any new system access grant (e.g. SAP Retail, Workforce Management) for the caller or a third party, (b) Any role-change or privilege-elevation request, (c) Password reset on an account flagged as privileged, executive, or holding elevated system entitlements, (d) Any request affecting a store's payment gateway configuration rather than a single terminal. The Voice Agent logs and routes these requests but takes no provisioning action itself; provisioning is completed by a human operator via the Identity & Access Management team after approval.

sections.heading: Excluded / Out-of-Scope Request Types
sections.content: The Voice Agent must not attempt password reset or access actions for: shared/generic store accounts, third-party vendor accounts, or any account where the caller is not the account owner and is not a verified manager/delegate acting on behalf of a named new starter. These fall outside the enumerated closed action set and must be redirected to the standard Identity & Access Management request channel.

sections.heading: PII Handling During Verification and Action Execution
sections.content: Caller name and employee ID are pseudonymised (stable tokens, e.g. PERSON_1, EMP_TOKEN_nnnn) before the transcript reaches the reasoning model. The tool proxy resolves pseudonyms to real identifiers only at the point of calling the target API (Entra ID / MIM or ITSM); the real identifier is never returned to the model or persisted in the transcript. Token-to-real-value mappings are held in an isolated, CMK-encrypted vault with a TTL matched to the associated ticket's lifecycle.

sections.heading: Escalation Guardrails
sections.content: Two consecutive failed intent resolutions on the same call trigger mandatory escalation to a human service desk agent, with full pseudonymised call context and transcript handed over. This is the sole automatic escalation trigger for the Voice Agent (no separate confidence-threshold escalation is defined for voice, unlike the Conversational Agent). A hard call timeout also applies regardless of intent-resolution outcome.
